newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU ministers to meet on Zaire crisis.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to meet on Zaire crisis.

text.p: European Union ministers are to hold an emergency meeting to look at how to help the hundreds of thousands of refugees in eastern Zaire, an Irish foreign ministry spokesman said on Thursday.

The meeting was requested by Belgium, the former colonial power of the central African country where more than a million Hutu refugees are caught up in fighting between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels.

The Irish foreign ministry spokesman said Belgium had asked Ireland, as EU president, to hold a meeting so Dublin has sent out invitations to its EU partners suggesting a meeting in Brussels on Thursday morning.
"In the interim, EU special envoy Aldo Ajello has been mediating in the area and has visited Kigali and Kinshasa and his efforts will continue," he said.

Belgian Secretary of State for Cooperation and Development Reginald Moreels said on Wednesday that he and Foreign Minister Eric Derycke had written to EU humanitarian aid commissioner Emma Bonino and the bloc's Irish presidency with the request.
Moreels said the conference of humanitarian aid, cooperation and development ministers should cover emergency aid to the region and address ways to find a political solution.
There needed to be an escorted return of refugees to their home countries, he said, with the escorting force ideally made up of troops from member states of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU).

He also urged the creation of corridors for aid to pass in the Goma-Bukavu-Uvira strip of eastern Zaire, secured by the OAU intervention troops. The EU should provide financial and logistical support.
